summary: Christoph Kleine works in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD (circa 1991-1995) and Habilitation (circa 1996-2001) from the University of Marburg, and held professorships at LMU Munich (2004-2008) and Leipzig University (circa 2008).

Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf was an indologist and historian/archaeologist. He held the Chair of Asian Anthropology at the University of London (circa 1951-1976) and was later attested as a professor at SOAS University of London in 1988.
Christophe Vielle is an Indologist who taught Sandra Smets. He served as a professor of Sanskrit at KU Leuven (attested 2009) and as a professor at Université catholique de Louvain (attested 2013).

Christopher André Holmboe studied at the University of Oslo (~1814-1818) and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy and Armand-Pierre Caussin de Perceval (1821). He worked in linguistics, Indology, and history/archaeology, serving at Oslo as Reader (1822) and Professor of Oriental Languages (1828).

Christopher Byrne is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. Supervised by Grace S. Fong and G. Victor Sōgen Hori, and taught by Robin D. S. Yates, he completed his PhD at McGill University (attested 2015).
Christopher D. Emms specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at McMaster University, where his doctoral supervisor was Shayne Clarke (attested 2012).

Christopher D. Wallis studied at the University of Rochester (BA), the University of Oxford (MPhil under Alexis Sanderson), and UC Berkeley (PhD, 2014, under Robert P. Goldman and Alexander von Rospatt). An Indologist, he was a guest lecturer at Naropa University in 2020.

Christopher Framarin studied philosophy at the University of Hawaii (MA, 2001) and the University of New Mexico (PhD, 2005). He works in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies, becoming associate professor in philosophy and religious studies at the University of Calgary (attested 2014).

Christopher Hatchell specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under academic mentor David Germano and committee members Paul Groner, Karen C. Lang, Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and Robert A. Hueckstedt.

Christopher I. Beckwith studied at Ohio State (~1964-1968) and Indiana University (~1974-1984) under Helmut Hoffmann and Thubten Jigme Norbu. Specializing in Tibetology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian studies, he held posts at Indiana University in 1982 and ~1986.

Christopher Ives is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He served as Assistant Professor of Religion at the University of Puget Sound (~1987-2001) and became professor and chair of religious studies at Stonehill College (~2001).

Christopher Jon Jensen studied at the University of Saskatchewan (BA), Kyoto University, and McMaster University (PhD, 2018), supervised by James A. Benn. His fields are religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies.

Christopher Kelley, a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies, earned his PhD from Columbia University. He founded the Columbia Society for Comparative Philosophy and has taught at Columbia University, The New School, and Brooklyn College.

Christopher Key Chapple specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He held posts at the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions (attested 1982), Stony Brook University (attested 1983), and Loyola Marymount University as Doshi Professor (attested 1998-2017).

Christopher Minkowski studied at Harvard College (~1973-1977) and Harvard University (~1981-1986). A scholar of Indology and religious studies, he held posts at Brown, Iowa, and Cornell before serving as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford and Balliol College (~2005-2023).
Christopher Pinney is an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. He held academic posts at the Australian National University (~1991-1993) and University College London (~1993).

Christopher S. George studied at Columbia University under Royal W. Weiler (1965) and with Geshe Wangyal and Padma Gyaltsen. In 1972, he founded the American Institute of Buddhist Studies, later serving as professor at the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions (attested 1982).

Christopher S. Queen is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. At Harvard University (~1989-2017), he served as Dean of Students for Continuing Education and lectured on the Study of Religion, Buddhism, and World Religions.
Chu-tsing Li studied at the University of Iowa (~1948-1955) and held a post at the University of Kansas (~1966-1990). He worked in the fields of history/archaeology and Sinology.

Chuan-ying Yen is a scholar in history/archaeology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Harvard University (attested 1986) under doctoral supervisor John M. Rosenfield, tutor Chu-tsing Li, and teacher John Hay.
